## Problem

The global sensitive-content masking preference is available inside Settings, but the main gallery has no readily accessible control for changing it. Users switching between private viewing, a shared workspace and screen sharing must interrupt browsing and navigate through the settings dialog.

The user raised this usability concern during the native application review. Source inspection confirms the preference is exposed in SettingsModal and passed from App.vue into VirtualGrid, while the gallery toolbar provides sorting, zoom and view-mode controls without a masking toggle.

## Environment and evidence

Omera 0.4.3, Windows development application on dev. Reviewed runtime baseline: [bdac8fb](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/commit/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5); subsequent merge a4ac24f changes issue templates/contribution documentation only.

- [Settings preference](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src/components/SettingsModal.vue#L844)
- [Gallery toolbar](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src/App.vue#L2356)
- [Current runtime masking state](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src/App.vue#L313)
- [Per-image reveal state](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src/components/VirtualGrid.vue#L85)

## Proposed interaction

Add a one-click toggle at a stable location in the main gallery toolbar, near the view-mode controls. Show both an icon and explicit localized state, such as **Masking on** / **Content visible**. The control should remain available without selecting an image and at normal/narrow window sizes.

Recommended preference model: Settings retains the startup default; the quick control changes the current viewing session. The interface should distinguish the active session state from the saved startup default.

Enabling masking should immediately conceal sensitive items again, including images temporarily revealed earlier in that session. Disabling masking should visibly indicate that content is exposed. This is a presentation control; it does not change an image's NSFW classification or the library's metadata.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Provide a discoverable, one-click toolbar control with clear current-state text.
- [ ] Apply the change immediately using the shared presentation state without rescanning, reclassifying or changing source files.
- [ ] Clear temporary reveal overrides when the user explicitly enables global masking.
- [ ] Make the control keyboard-operable, expose its toggle state to assistive technology, and provide a documented shortcut that respects focused inputs and modal dialogs.
- [ ] Localize all control text and keep the action available at narrow widths and without a selection.
- [ ] Make session/startup-default behavior explicit and test navigation, view changes and previously revealed items.

## Scope and dependencies

This issue covers quick access and feedback for the masking control. Existing Table-mode enforcement is tracked in #252, and classification false positives in #296. Those reports remain separate; the toolbar control must not imply that unresolved presentation surfaces are protected.

Implementation PRs target dev. Follow the repository's presentation, virtualization and configuration compatibility rules. This is a UX proposal; no implementation is included in this report.

## Summary

**Reproduced against the production extractor and classifier.** A PNG with positive prompt landscape, mountain, daylight and negative prompt nsfw, nude is classified NSFW. detect_nsfw_from_metadata searches meta.raw/parameters as undifferentiated text, so terms the generator was told to exclude become positive classification signals.

## Environment and evidence

Omera 0.4.3; Windows; dev at [bdac8fb](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/commit/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5), SQLite schema 15. - [crates/omera-metadata/src/lib.rs:214](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/crates/omera-metadata/src/lib.rs#L214)

## Reproduction or validation

1. Create a synthetic solid-color PNG carrying A1111 parameters with a safe positive prompt and nsfw/nude only in Negative prompt.
2. Extract metadata with extract_metadata(Container::Png, path).
3. Call detect_nsfw_from_metadata; it returns true even though the positive prompt contains no NSFW indicator.

Code-confirmed scenarios above are validation instructions unless the summary explicitly states that the scenario was executed. No destructive real-library or live remote-provider test is implied.

## Expected behavior

Negative prompt exclusions do not count as positive NSFW signals.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Classify structured positive prompt/rating fields instead of undifferentiated raw parameter text.
- [ ] Exclude negative-prompt content from positive classification.
- [ ] Test safe positive/adult-negative, adult-positive/safe-negative and explicit rating fields while preserving user overrides.

## Scope

This issue covers one topic: Negative prompt exclusions trigger false-positive NSFW classification. Implementation PRs target dev. Preserve source data and follow the lead-owned persistence/security/cleanup boundaries in [ENGINEERING_HANDOFF.md](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/docs/ENGINEERING_HANDOFF.md).

The real library's classification counts prompted this investigation, but this report does not claim that every flagged real image is a false positive.

## Synthetic production-function reproduction

Save this as the review harness's `src/lib.rs` using the Cargo manifest published in #237. Run `cargo test --manifest-path docs/reviews/repro-2026-10-05/Cargo.toml --target-dir target --lib negative_prompt_exclusions`. It fails on the reviewed baseline; no sensitive media is needed.

```rust
#[test]
fn negative_prompt_exclusions_must_not_classify_a_safe_prompt_as_nsfw() {
    let temp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let path = temp.path().join("safe-landscape.png");
    let mut encoder = png::Encoder::new(std::fs::File::create(&path).unwrap(), 16, 16);
    encoder.set_color(png::ColorType::Rgb);
    encoder.set_depth(png::BitDepth::Eight);
    encoder.add_text_chunk("parameters".into(), "landscape, mountain, daylight\nNegative prompt: nsfw, nude\nSteps: 20, Sampler: Euler, Seed: 123, Size: 16x16".into()).unwrap();
    encoder.write_header().unwrap().write_image_data(&vec![120; 16 * 16 * 3]).unwrap();
    let metadata = omera_metadata::extract_metadata(omera_domain::Container::Png, &path).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(metadata.prompt.as_deref(), Some("landscape, mountain, daylight"));
    assert!(!omera_metadata::detect_nsfw_from_metadata(&metadata));
}
```

## Controlled production-class concurrency probe

Save the following as `docs/reviews/repro-2026-10-05/history-concurrency.test.mjs`, then run `pnpm exec tsx --test docs/reviews/repro-2026-10-05/history-concurrency.test.mjs`. The assertion fails with peak 2 instead of 1. The barrier is released before the assertion, so the test leaves no pending operations.

```js
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { ActionHistory } from '../../../src/utils/history.ts';

test('overlapping undo requests must not run commands concurrently', async () => {
  const history = new ActionHistory();
  let active = 0;
  let peak = 0;
  let release;
  const barrier = new Promise(resolve => { release = resolve; });
  const command = name => ({
    name, execute: async () => {},
    undo: async () => { active += 1; peak = Math.max(peak, active); await barrier; active -= 1; },
  });
  await history.execute(command('A'));
  await history.execute(command('B'));
  const first = history.undo();
  const second = history.undo();
  const observed = peak;
  release();
  await Promise.allSettled([first, second]);
  assert.equal(observed, 1, 'History ran two undo commands concurrently');
});

```

### Description
In `src/components/VirtualGrid.vue` (lines 759–768), when an indexed video asset does not yet have a disk thumbnail, the grid mounts a native HTML5 `<video>` element for every visible card:

```html

  v-else-if="isVideoContainer(file.container)"
```

In directories containing dozens of video files (e.g., AnimateDiff, SVD, or screen captures), virtual scrolling renders 30 to 50 active `<video preload="metadata">` instances simultaneously.

On Windows WebView2 (Chromium), hardware accelerated video decoders (D3D11 / NVDEC) have strict concurrency limits (typically 16–32 simultaneous decoder contexts). When this limit is exceeded:

### Proposed Solution
1. Never mount native `<video>` elements as poster thumbnails in `VirtualGrid`.
2. Display a lightweight static video placeholder icon with duration badge until the background Rust thumbnailer generates a static WebP thumbnail.

### Description
In `src-tauri/src/cloud_sync.rs`, fourteen separate locations call `.lock().unwrap()` on the shared `sync_state` mutex across multi-threaded worker pools:

```rust
// Lines 111, 127, 140, 170, 177, 182, 236, 262, 281, 294, 313, 336, 346, 529
let mut state = self.state.lock().unwrap();
```

### Risk & Failure Mechanism
In multi-threaded Rust applications, if any worker thread panics during cloud synchronization (e.g. unexpected socket disconnect, network timeout, S3/WebDAV authentication failure, or token bucket overflow), the mutex becomes **poisoned**.

Once poisoned, every subsequent call to `cloud_sync_cancel`, `cloud_sync_get_progress`, `cloud_sync_get_summary`, or `cloud_sync_start` immediately panics on `.unwrap()`, bringing down the entire desktop application process.

### Proposed Solution
Replace all 14 `.lock().unwrap()` occurrences with safe error propagation:
```rust
let mut state = self.state.lock().map_err(|e| format!("Cloud sync mutex poisoned: {e}"))?;
```
Or use a resilient lock helper that recovers from poisoned states gracefully.

### Environment
- **App Version**: Omera v0.4.3
- **Component**: `src-tauri/src/cloud_sync.rs`

### Description
Tauri 2 commands marked with `pub async fn` execute on Tokio runtime worker threads. CPU-bound and blocking synchronous operations executed without `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` starve the async runtime, delaying IPC message delivery, timers, and internal event loops.

### Offending Synchronous Implementations in `async fn` Commands:
1. **`export_files_batch` (`src-tauri/src/commands.rs:1731–1742`)**:
   Marked `pub async fn`, but calls `execute_batch_export` synchronously on Tokio threads, running multi-format image encoding (AVIF, WebP, JPEG) and ZIP writing directly on the async reactor.
2. **`transform_library_files_batch` (`src-tauri/src/commands.rs:1761–1810`)**:
   Marked `pub async fn`, but invokes `execute_library_batch_transform` synchronously on the Tokio runtime thread, looping through hundreds of image decodes and encodings.
3. **`batch_auto_tag_files` (`src-tauri/src/commands.rs:2671–2715`)**:
   Marked `pub async fn`, but executes a synchronous `for fid in file_ids` loop directly on the async worker thread, performing CPU image decoding and ONNX neural network inference per file without yielding.
4. **Synchronous HTTP Requests**:
   `send_to_webui` (`commands.rs:4423`) uses synchronous `ureq` with a 30-second read timeout, blocking worker threads during slow model generation requests.

### Proposed Solution
Wrap all CPU-heavy transcoding, multi-file batch loops, and blocking I/O calls in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` (or delegate to Rayon worker thread pools), ensuring Tokio async runtime threads remain free for responsive IPC handling.

### Environment

### Description
In creative digital asset managers (such as Eagle, Lightroom, and Apple Photos), users frequently perform rapid, high-volume library curation actions. In Omera, there is **zero Undo / Redo infrastructure** across the entire application.

### Affected High-Impact Workflows
The following operations are instantaneous, irreversible, and have no undo mechanism:
1. **Batch Rating**: Rating hundreds of selected files (`App.vue:942–965`). An accidental keypress (`0` instead of `5`) wipes out ratings for large selections permanently.
2. **Batch Favorite / NSFW Toggling**: (`App.vue:1428–1476`).
3. **Batch Tagging / Untagging**: (`App.vue:1406–1413`).
4. **Physical File Moves**: Moving selected files between physical folders (`App.vue:1836–1846`).
5. **Image Stacking & Auto-Stacking**: Merging and collapsing stacks (`App.vue:999–1059`).
6. **Draft Culling**: Deleting lower-rated drafts inside stacks (`App.vue:1304–1319`).

### Proposed Solution
1. Introduce a client-side command pattern engine (`src/utils/history.ts`):
   - `ActionHistory` stack managing reversible action objects with `execute()`, `undo()`, and `redo()`.
2. Implement reversible action commands:
   - `BatchRateCommand`, `BatchTagCommand`, `BatchFavoriteCommand`, `FileMoveCommand`, `StackCommand`.
3. Bind standard keyboard shortcuts:
   - `Ctrl+Z` / `Cmd+Z` for Undo.
   - `Ctrl+Y` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` for Redo.
4. Display brief undo confirmation toasts when destructive actions occur.

### Environment
- **App Version**: Omera v0.4.3
- **Components**: `src/App.vue`, `src/utils/`

body:
### Description
To safeguard authentic generation metadata (original prompts from SD WebUI, ComfyUI, NovelAI, etc.) against accidental corruption, overwriting, or dilution by automated taggers, introduce a strict **Prompt Immutability & Protection Policy** across the UI and backend.

### Core Safeguards & Requirements

1. **Lock and Hide Prompt Interrogation When Prompt Already Exists**:
   - For images that already possess non-empty prompt metadata (`metadata.prompt` is not null or whitespace):
     - **Hide Interrogation Entry**: Do NOT display "Interrogate Prompt" action buttons or prompt-writing checkboxes for that image.
     - **Read-Only Lock**: Existing prompt text must be locked against accidental re-interrogation, inline editing, or automated overwriting.
   - Images without existing prompts (`metadata.prompt` is empty / null) continue to permit prompt interrogation.

2. **Decouple Auto-Tagging from Prompt Interrogation**:
   - Explicitly separate:
     - **`Auto-Tag to Library Tags`**: Inserts into SQLite `tag` / `file_tag` tables for gallery filtering and categorizing. Always available and non-destructive.
     - **`Interrogate Prompt`**: Writes comma-separated token strings into `metadata.prompt`. Conditionally visible and locked if a prompt exists.

3. **Developer Settings Override Toggle**:
   - In `SettingsModal.vue`, introduce a **"Developer Options"** / "Advanced" tab or section.
   - Include a toggle:
     - **`Allow Modifying and Overwriting Existing Prompts`**
     - Default: `false` (Disabled / Protected).
   - Only when a power user or dataset trainer explicitly activates this developer toggle will the UI and backend unlock prompt re-interrogation, editing, and overwriting on images with existing prompt data.

### Proposed Architecture & Flow
1. **Config Key**:
   Add `allow_override_existing_prompt: boolean` (default: `false`) in both `src/utils/config.ts` and `src-tauri/src/commands.rs`.
2. **UI Interactivity**:
   - In `InspectorPane.vue`, render prompt as locked/read-only unless developer mode override is enabled.
   - In `AutoTagModal.vue`, if target image has existing prompt and developer toggle is disabled, hide or disable the prompt-writing option with an informative tooltip ("Original prompt protected. Enable in Developer Settings to overwrite").
3. **Backend Validation**:
   - In `auto_tag_file` and `batch_auto_tag_files`, refuse to overwrite non-empty `metadata.prompt` unless `allow_override_existing_prompt` flag is true in the request config.

### References
- Complements and expands upon issue #189.

### Environment
- **App Version**: Omera v0.4.3
- **Components**: `src/components/SettingsModal.vue`, `src/components/AutoTagModal.vue`, `src/components/InspectorPane.vue`, `src-tauri/src/commands.rs`
title: [Feature/Safety] Prompt protection safeguards: lock non-empty prompts against interrogation/overwrite and gate modifications behind Developer Settings

### Description
In `src/components/BatchActionBar.vue`, the logic to collapse secondary batch action buttons into the "More" dropdown is currently implemented via a hardcoded pixel threshold:

```ts
resizeObserver = new ResizeObserver((entries) => {
  for (const entry of entries) {
    const width = entry.contentRect.width;
    isCompact.value = width < 920;
  }
});
```

### Problems Identified
1. **Dynamic Content Width Variations**:
   - The total width required by the action bar is not constant. When stacked images are selected, the "Cull Drafts" (`cullDrafts`) button is conditionally rendered, increasing the required width.
2. **Internationalization (i18n) Text Expansion**:
   - In languages like German, French, or Spanish, button text expands by 30% to 50% compared to English. The full button row easily requires up to **1250px**.
3. **Severe Button Puncturing & Overflow Defect**:
   - In viewports between 920px and ~1200px (e.g. the standard 1280px desktop window with both the left sidebar and right inspector panel opened), `isCompact` remains `false`.
   - The inline buttons overflow the capsule container: buttons puncture through the right rounded boundary (`border-radius: 999px`), causing clipping, while trailing actions (like Move, Copy, Export, Trash) are pushed completely off-screen or underneath adjacent panels.

### Proposed Solution
Replace the brittle static `width < 920` check with dynamic overflow detection or responsive container adaptation:
1. **Dynamic ScrollWidth Measurement**:
   Check whether the contents overflow the container (`barRef.scrollWidth > barRef.clientWidth`). When an overflow is detected, automatically switch to compact mode (`isCompact = true`).
2. **Adaptive Flex Wrap / Priority Overflow**:
   Or implement a dynamic priority-based overflow container where buttons that do not fit into the available width automatically spill into the "More" menu, guaranteeing that buttons will never puncture or clip the capsule border regardless of language, font scaling, or window size.

### Environment
- **App Version**: Omera v0.4.3
- **Component**: `src/components/BatchActionBar.vue`

### Description
In `src-tauri/src/commands.rs`, `batch_auto_tag_files` processes multi-selected files using a sequential, synchronous loop across all requested file IDs:

```rust
pub async fn batch_auto_tag_files(
    file_ids: Vec<i64>,
    config: TaggerConfig,
    state: State<'_, AppState>,
) -> Result<BatchTagResult, String> {
    let mut processed_files = 0;
    let mut tags_added = 0;

    for fid in file_ids {
        // Synchronous ONNX inference & database inserts per file
        ...
    }

    Ok(BatchTagResult { processed_files, tags_added })
}
```

### Problems Identified
1. **No Cancellation Mechanism**: Unlike model downloads (`cancel_tagger_download`), there is no `AtomicBool` cancellation flag checked inside the iteration. If a user triggers batch tagging across hundreds or thousands of files, the background task cannot be halted or aborted without terminating the entire application.
2. **Missing Real-Time Progress Events**: No granular progress updates (e.g. `current / total`, percentage, current filename) are emitted to the frontend during execution. The frontend modal remains stuck on a generic disabled state with no progress feedback.
3. **No Failure Resilience or Error Reporting**: If individual images fail to decode or predict, there is no granular failure visibility or ability to skip/retry failed items.

### Proposed Solution: BatchAutoTagController
Design and implement a structured batch tagger pipeline mirroring the architecture of `ClipIndexingController`:
1. **Backend (`src-tauri/src/commands.rs`)**:
   - Introduce an `AtomicBool` cancel flag (`batch_tagger_cancel`) in `AppState`.
   - Expose a `cancel_batch_auto_tag` Tauri command.
   - Emit periodic `tagger-batch-progress` events (payload: `current`, `total`, `percent`, `current_file`, `success_count`, `failure_count`).
   - Run inference in bounded background chunks, checking the cancel token before each file.
2. **Frontend (`src/components/AutoTagModal.vue` & TypeScript Controller)**:
   - Provide real-time progress bar, percentage display, and current processing filename.
   - Provide an immediate `Cancel` button to gracefully stop batch processing.
   - Display a completion summary highlighting succeeded vs failed items with retry capability.

### Environment
- **App Version**: Omera v0.4.3
- **Components**: `src-tauri/src/commands.rs`, `src/components/AutoTagModal.vue`

### Description
Whenever the **WD14 AI Auto-Tagger modal (`AutoTagModal.vue`)** is opened, it consistently displays the "No WD14 tagger model detected" empty prompt and requests the user to download the recommended model (388MB) again, even when the model (`model.onnx` and `selected_tags.csv`) has already been fully downloaded and exists in `%APPDATA%/com.berryuiki.omera/models/wd14/wd-v1-4-convnext-tagger-v2/`.

### Root Cause Analysis
In `src/App.vue`, `AutoTagModal` is conditionally rendered with `v-if="autoTagModalOpen"`:
```vue
<AutoTagModal
  v-if="autoTagModalOpen"
  :show="autoTagModalOpen"
  ...
/>
```
In `src/components/AutoTagModal.vue`:
1. `loadModelList()` is invoked exclusively within a non-immediate watcher on `props.show`:
   ```ts
   watch(
     () => props.show,
     (val) => {
       if (val) {
         message.value = null;
         predictions.value = [];
         void loadModelList();
       }
     },
   );
   ```
2. Because of `v-if`, the component is mounted each time the modal opens. On initial mount, `props.show` is already initialized to `true`.
3. In Vue 3, `watch()` does not execute upon component initialization unless `{ immediate: true }` is supplied.
4. `onMounted()` does not invoke `loadModelList()`.
5. Consequently, `models.value` remains an empty array (`[]`).
6. Because `models.length === 0`, the template evaluates the fallback branch:
   ```vue
   <div v-else-if="models.length === 0" class="section-box empty-model-box">
   ```
   displaying the initial setup card and asking the user to re-download the ~388MB model files on every open.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open the WD14 Auto-Tagger modal and click "Download Recommended Model" to download `wd-v1-4-convnext-tagger-v2`. Wait for download completion (model status becomes ready).
2. Close the modal dialog.
3. Reopen the Auto-Tagger modal on the same or another image.
4. Observe the modal body.

### Expected Behavior
- The modal should discover and list existing downloaded models in `%APPDATA%/com.berryuiki.omera/models/wd14/` immediately upon mounting (`onMounted` or `{ immediate: true }` on the watcher).
- The previously downloaded model should be selected and loaded without prompting to download again.

### Actual Behavior
- The modal displays "No WD14 tagger model detected" and prompts the user to download the 388MB model every time it opens.

### Environment
- **App Version**: Omera v0.4.3
- **OS**: Windows 11
- **Component**: `src/components/AutoTagModal.vue`, `src/App.vue`

### Description
In the **WD14 AI Auto-Tagger modal (`AutoTagModal.vue`)**, several UI layout and state representation defects occur:

1. **Duplicate Identical Action Buttons in Footer During Execution**:
   When multiple files are selected (`selectedFileCount > 1`), the modal footer displays both the batch apply button (`applyToBatch`) and current file apply button (`applyToCurrent`). Both buttons bind to the shared loading flag `isApplying`. When tagging begins, both buttons simultaneously switch their labels to `t.autoTagModal.tagging` ("Tagging in progress..."). This results in two adjacent, disabled buttons with completely identical text, giving the impression of duplicated/misplaced elements and concealing which action was initiated.
2. **Missing Progress & Interruption State in Batch Tagging**:
   When batch tagging a large selection of files (e.g., 87 files), the process can take significant time with no progress indicator, counter, or cancel button in the modal footer while both buttons are stuck in the identical disabled state.
3. **Model Name Truncation / Misidentification**:
   The active model status pill displays `● Model Ready: model` instead of the actual model identifier (e.g. `wd-v1-4-convnext-tagger-v2`), caused by backend `Wd14Tagger::load` deriving the model name from `model_path.file_stem()`, which resolves to generic `"model"` for `model.onnx`.
4. **Floating Batch Action Bar Visibility Under Modal Backdrop**:
   The floating `BatchActionBar` at the bottom of the viewport remains rendered behind the modal backdrop blur rather than being cleanly dismissed or hidden when modal overlays are active.

### Steps to Reproduce

# Omera storage evolution

Status: design direction; optimizations require measurements and append-only migrations.

## Decision

Retain embedded SQLite with WAL as the authoritative local library, renamed to `omera.db`. The current application already relies on relational transactions for files, folders, tags, albums, stacks, and recovery. Renaming or replacing the engine alone does not make those workloads faster. Remote MySQL/PostgreSQL support is not implemented end to end and must not be advertised as available.

Keep original media on disk, large model weights outside the database, and thumbnails in a disposable bounded disk cache. Preserve existing IDs, relationships, metadata, embeddings, and schema version during identity migration. Do not rebuild a user's library from a filesystem scan as a substitute for migration.

## Workload-driven changes

| Workload | Proposed change | Evidence required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gallery pages | Small typed projections, stable keyset cursors with ID tie-breaks, indexes matching scope and ordering | EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN and first/deep-page p50/p95 latency |
| Metadata filters | Extract frequently queried fields into typed indexed columns or a one-to-one metadata table; keep full source JSON separately | Lower page/filter latency and IPC size without lost search semantics |
| Full-text search | Evaluate SQLite FTS5 alongside existing behavior | Multilingual tokenization, substring expectations, update cost, index size and correctness |
| Sidebar totals | Aggregate counts in bounded query groups and invalidate by mutation category | Startup query count and refresh latency, with accurate counts |
| Thumbnail bookkeeping | Reuse worker connections, coalesce access/budget writes, bound eviction batches | Decode throughput, lock wait and write amplification |
| Semantic search | Bounded top-k selection and bulk hydration first; evaluate optional vector indexes later | Exact-search baseline, recall@k, memory, latency and packaging cost |
| Background indexing | Short bounded write transactions and explicit busy handling; separate background reads | UI latency while scan/inference/cache jobs run together |

Do not add indexes for every column or introduce a second authoritative database without measurements. Separating cache metadata into another SQLite database may reduce contention, but also loses cross-database foreign-key guarantees and complicates recovery; retain the existing layout until contention measurements justify it. Optional vector indexes must be rebuildable derivatives of versioned authoritative embeddings.

## Schema and migration rules

- Applied migrations remain unchanged and ordered. Append new migrations in the storage crate; crate renaming moves the file without rewriting its history.
- Backfill large new structures in bounded resumable batches. Do not expose incomplete indexes as complete search results. Define schema compatibility and recovery before switching readers.
- Use foreign keys, uniqueness constraints, and explicit version/revision fields where required by actual ownership. Verify `integrity_check` and `foreign_key_check` on migrated copies.
- Store migration receipts outside the source database so failure never requires modifying the only good copy. Legacy discovery and cleanup follow [OMERA_MIGRATION.md](OMERA_MIGRATION.md).
- Keep authoritative databases on local storage; media may reside on network shares. A shared multi-user service is a separate future architecture, not a connection-string toggle.

## Benchmark and acceptance plan

Benchmark production query and cache functions on reproducible 1k, 10k, 50k and 100k fixtures; add 500k where resources permit. Include metadata-heavy rows, sparse fields, multiple tags/albums, stacked files, cold/warm caches, concurrent indexing, and deep pagination. Record hardware, commit, dataset generation, query plans, database/index bytes, peak memory, startup-to-first-page time, IPC bytes and p50/p95 latency.

Compare against the same baseline and publish results in `docs/benchmarks/`. A redesign is accepted only when correctness tests pass and measured target workloads improve without material startup, write, memory, or recovery regressions. Synthetic loops that do not exercise production functions are not evidence. No engine change or unmeasured speedup is promised by this plan.

# Omera identity and pre-1.0 migration contract

Status: accepted product direction; implementation and release verification pending.

## Target identity

The product is Omera. The application identifier is `com.berryuiki.omera` and the canonical repository is `https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera`. Use `omera` for the executable/package name, `omera-*` for workspace crates, `omera_*` for local settings, `Omera` for the credential service, and `omera.db` for the active library database. Release artifacts, websites, CI, examples, translations, exported branding, and documentation must use the new identity. Keep BerryUIKI attribution and license history intact.

Legacy identifiers are compatibility inputs, not active write destinations. Centralize them in migration code rather than scattering fallback writes throughout the application. Retain the released schema history unchanged, even where historical SQL or fixtures contain legacy names.

Changing the application identifier changes platform data locations and may change WebView storage origins, installer identity, permissions, and macOS sandbox access. A successful rename of source strings alone does not demonstrate migration compatibility.

## Compatibility window

Every release before 1.0.0 must check known legacy locations and allow migration from supported Berry libraries, settings, and backup archives. A durable migration receipt prevents repeated import of the same source. Discovery still runs when new legacy data appears. Opening an existing Omera library always takes precedence over automatic legacy import.

Do not reset the application version or SQLite schema version for the rename. Before 1.0.0, review telemetry-free test evidence and document the supported import path for 1.0.0; reaching 1.0.0 never authorizes automatic deletion of old data.

## Startup migration protocol

1. Resolve the new application data directory and platform-specific legacy directories for `com.berryuiki.berryaistudio`, including supported historical layouts. Reject symlinks/reparse points that escape approved roots. Detect concurrent legacy writers and ask the user to close the old application before activation or cleanup.
2. Discover database, configuration, credentials, model files, thumbnail cache, and WebView settings separately. Show source paths, library counts, estimated space, and conflicts. If multiple libraries exist or Omera already has a library, require a source choice or explicit import; never silently overwrite or combine unrelated file IDs.
3. Create a migration receipt with source identity, source schema version, destination, per-artifact state, and validation results. Never put secrets in the receipt. Acquire a migration lock and use a staging directory on the destination volume.
4. Snapshot SQLite through its backup API so committed WAL data is included. Never copy only a live `.db`, rename a live database, or delete its WAL/SHM files. Preserve the original. Validate integrity, foreign keys, supported schema version, entity counts and associations; apply append-only migrations to the staged copy. Reject newer unsupported schemas without modifying them.
5. Migrate configuration with compatible defaults and explicit old-to-new key mappings. A present Omera value wins over a legacy value, including `false`, `0`, and empty values. Write credentials to the new OS credential service and verify retrieval before marking them migrated; retain old entries until cleanup approval.
6. Publish validated `omera.db` and configuration atomically per file. The receipt makes the multi-file operation resumable; do not claim a filesystem-wide atomic transaction. Activate only when required artifacts are complete. Start database connections, watchers, and inference workers after activation. On failure, preserve sources and staging evidence and offer retry or source selection, not silent creation of an empty replacement library.
7. Render the migrated SQLite library before optional scans or cache work. Copy models only when verified and needed. Thumbnails are disposable: rebuild lazily or migrate valid entries and rewrite cache paths. Do not retain active references to caches scheduled for cleanup.

WebView localStorage may be inaccessible from the new identifier. Reading `berry_*` from the new origin alone is insufficient. Support a legacy-app export/bridge or explicit import of a versioned settings export where direct access is unavailable. Do not assume raw WebView profile databases can safely be edited. Backend `config.json` remains authoritative after migration.

## Cleanup requires a separate user decision

After migration succeeds and Omera reopens and reads the destination successfully, show a localized, dismissible cleanup prompt with the exact old paths, categories, and sizes. Offer **Keep old data** (default), **Review cleanup**, and a later entry in settings. Record refusal without repeatedly prompting on every launch.

Cleanup is restricted to verified legacy application-owned files listed in the receipt. Revalidate paths and source revisions immediately before cleanup. Never delete linked media, user-selected managed vaults, external folders, arbitrary backups, or shared model directories as part of an application-data cleanup. If a legacy root contains user assets, explicitly exclude them and explain why some files remain.

Require renewed confirmation if the source changed after migration. Use OS trash for eligible files; report partial failures and retain a retryable receipt. Never fall back to permanent deletion. Old credential entries may be removed only when the new entries are readable and their deletion is explicitly included in the approved cleanup scope. Application uninstall and legacy binary removal are separate installer actions, not recursive data-directory cleanup.

## Installer and update compatibility

- Use the Omera repository in update checks, verified-download allowlists, release workflows, links, and signing documentation. Keep established signing keys where available; key rotation requires its own trust transition. Missing signing credentials block automatic installation, not verification bypass.
- Match assets by OS, architecture, and installer type. Never select the first release asset as a fallback. Validate the signature again before execution.
- Inspect actual released installers to determine old executable names, NSIS uninstall entries, MSI UpgradeCode (when applicable), shortcuts, and installation scope. New identity requires explicit legacy detection and replacement handling. Test elevation boundaries and do not remove the old installation until migration/recovery access is secured.
- macOS Bundle ID changes require new provisioning/App Store identity where applicable. A sandboxed new identity may not read the old container automatically; provide user-mediated import/export. Do not present this as an ordinary in-place App Store update.
- Older clients may use the redirected GitHub URL but still enforce old download URLs or select assets incorrectly. Test direct upgrade from every supported published version, including users who skip a bridge release. Where automatic upgrade is impossible, provide a manual installer and migration instructions.
- Publish only after Berry -> Omera -> next Omera upgrade tests pass on every supported target. Keep version numbers increasing and retain recovery snapshots; binary downgrade is not a safe database rollback after schema upgrades.

## Delivery and verification

1. Update documentation and track migration/release/storage tasks in GitHub issues.
2. Implement and test migration/cleanup services before switching the runtime identity.
3. Rename application, packages, crates, UI strings, settings, database, CI, and release artifacts; allow legacy strings only in migration code, fixtures, and historical records.
4. Complete the repository review fixes and regression coverage, then run the required build, frontend, formatting, Clippy, and Rust suites.
5. Exercise fresh install, legacy-only install, existing Omera plus legacy data, concurrent legacy app, full disk, interrupted migration at each stage, corrupt/future schema, WAL-resident changes, inaccessible sandbox data, credential failures, cleanup declined/approved/partial failure, and repeated startup. Verify user data and associations before and after migration.
6. Manually verify all gallery modes and accessibility, and test real signed installers and the next-update path. Do not mark issues complete based only on a renamed development build.

See [STORAGE_EVOLUTION.md](STORAGE_EVOLUTION.md) for storage decisions and [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md) for release gates.

### Summary
Currently, updating the application version requires manually modifying multiple scattered files across frontend, backend, and build configurations (`package.json`, root `Cargo.toml`, `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, and fallback literals in `App.vue`). This creates duplication, risk of version drift, and manual friction during release workflows.

### Proposed Architecture

1. **Native Tauri Version Reference**:
   Configure `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` to natively reference `package.json`:
   ```json
   "version": "../package.json"
   ```
   Tauri automatically extracts the version from `package.json` at build time, eliminating manual edits to `tauri.conf.json`.

2. **Compile-Time Frontend Injection in Vite**:
   Inject `__APP_VERSION__` in `vite.config.ts`:
   ```typescript
   define: {
     __APP_VERSION__: JSON.stringify(process.env.npm_package_version),
   }
   ```
   Replace hardcoded string fallbacks (e.g. in `App.vue`) with `__APP_VERSION__`, eliminating runtime RPC delay or fallback drift.

3. **Backend Dynamic Package Version**:
   Verify and preserve Rust commands using `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, which dynamically reads `[workspace.package].version` from `Cargo.toml`.

4. **Single-Command Version Synchronization**:
   Provide a unified script (`scripts/bump-version.mjs` / `pnpm run bump <version>`) that simultaneously updates `package.json` and root `Cargo.toml`, followed by updating `Cargo.lock`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Set `"version": "../package.json"` in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`.
- [ ] Define `__APP_VERSION__` in `vite.config.ts` and declare it in global types.
- [ ] Replace hardcoded version fallbacks in `src/App.vue`.
- [ ] Add `pnpm run bump <version>` script to synchronize frontend and Rust workspace manifests in one shot.

### Summary
When resizing the application window or expanding/collapsing sidebars, gallery card resizing is not fluid. Cards remain strictly clamped to `itemMinWidth`, leaving large 100–200px empty blank voids on the right side of the canvas until a new column threshold is abruptly reached. In contrast, modern asset managers (e.g. Eagle) smoothly stretch cards across the full container width to fill every row evenly.

### Reproduction Steps
1. Open the gallery in Grid or Masonry mode.
2. Slowly drag the window border or toggle the left/right sidebars.
3. Observe that cards stay at fixed widths, causing a wide empty gap on the right margin.
4. Once the window width crosses a column boundary, the layout abruptly jumps and snaps to an extra column.

### Root Cause Analysis & Evidence
- In [src/components/VirtualGrid.vue#L185-L188](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Berry-AI-Studio/blob/dev/src/components/VirtualGrid.vue#L185-L188):
  ```typescript
  const itemWidth = computed(() => {
    if (containerWidth.value <= 0) return props.itemMinWidth;
    return Math.max(1, Math.min(props.itemMinWidth, containerWidth.value));
  });
  ```
- And in template [VirtualGrid.vue#L605](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Berry-AI-Studio/blob/dev/src/components/VirtualGrid.vue#L605):
  ```html
  gridTemplateColumns: layout === 'grid' ? `repeat(${cols}, ${itemWidth}px)` : undefined
  ```
  Because `itemWidth` is locked to `props.itemMinWidth`, leftover space `containerWidth - (cols * itemWidth + (cols - 1) * gap)` is never distributed among the columns, creating empty black margins on the right.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dynamically compute column widths as `(containerWidth - (cols - 1) * gap) / cols` so cards fill the entire row without right-hand blank margins.
- [ ] Ensure smooth resizing transitions during window and sidebar animations.
- [ ] Preserve virtualization performance rules during continuous resize.

### Summary
In light theme, multiple UI components suffer from severe contrast degradation and incomplete theme adaptation. Specifically, native `<select>` dropdown option popups render with white/near-white text on light backgrounds in Windows WebView2, rendering options illegible. ### Reproduction Steps

Images generated via ComfyUI using Flux workflows (e.g. `CLIPTextEncodeFlux`), string concatenation / logic nodes (e.g. `ComfyUI-Easy-Use` nodes like `easy promptConcat` and `easy positive`), or node graph links fail to display prompts in Berry AI Studio. ### Summary
Opening the "Prompt & Metadata Insights" modal (`PromptStatsModal`) immediately fails with a runtime Tauri RPC serialization error. Furthermore, clicking the window close button (`✕`), the bottom action button (`Done`), or pressing `Escape` fails to dismiss the modal, deadlocking the user interface until the entire application is reloaded.

### Reproduction Steps
1. Launch Berry AI Studio and load an indexed library.
2. Open the Insights modal via top menu (`Tools` -> `Prompt Insights & Frequency Statistics...`) or bottom sidebar button.
3. Observe the red error message in the center:
   `invalid args 'isNegative' for command 'get_prompt_stats': command get_prompt_stats missing required key isNegative`
4. Click the `✕` close button in the top right or the `Done` button in the bottom right.
5. Press the `Escape` key on the keyboard.
6. The modal remains stuck on screen and cannot be closed.

### Root Cause Analysis & Evidence
1. **RPC Signature Mismatch**:
   - Backend definition in [src-tauri/src/commands.rs#L699](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Berry-AI-Studio/blob/dev/src-tauri/src/commands.rs#L699):
     ```rust
     #[tauri::command]
     pub fn get_prompt_stats(
         is_negative: bool,
         limit: usize,
         state: State<'_, AppState>,
     ) -> Result<Vec<PromptStat>, String>
     ```
   - Frontend caller in [src/components/PromptStatsModal.vue#L25](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Berry-AI-Studio/blob/dev/src/components/PromptStatsModal.vue#L25):
     ```typescript
     stats.value = await invoke<PromptStats>("get_prompt_stats", { limit: 40 });
     ```
     Missing required argument `isNegative` (camelCase for `is_negative`), and expects `PromptStats` instead of `PromptStat[]`.
2. **Event Name Mismatch Causing Close Deadlock**:
   - `PromptStatsModal.vue` emits `update:open`:
     ```typescript
     function close() {
       emit("update:open", false);
     }
     ```
   - Parent component [src/App.vue#L2170](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Berry-AI-Studio/blob/dev/src/App.vue#L2170) listens to `@close`:
     ```html
     <PromptStatsModal
       v-if="promptStatsModalOpen"
       :open="promptStatsModalOpen"
       @close="promptStatsModalOpen = false"
       @apply-search="onApplyStatsSearch"
     />
     ```
     Because the event names do not match and `v-model:open` is not used, the close signal is dropped.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Align `get_prompt_stats` RPC invocation with backend parameters (`isNegative: false/true`, `limit`), or aggregate stats across tabs appropriately.
- [ ] Align modal close event contract: ensure `PromptStatsModal` emits `close` (or `App.vue` binds `v-model:open="promptStatsModalOpen"` and handles `@close`).
- [ ] Verify that clicking `✕`, clicking `Done`, pressing `Esc`, or clicking the backdrop cleanly dismisses the modal.

- Encapsulate detail caching and mutation invalidation in one composable/service.

- Test select A, mutate A, select B, reselect A; also update A's source revision while it remains selected.
- Make eviction behavior match documented LRU semantics.

## Summary and actual behavior

**Reproduced and code-confirmed.** [cloud_backup.rs:903](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/cloud_backup.rs#L903) makes a raw rollback copy of only the live main database, ignores backup errors, and copies the restored file directly over the active database. [commands.rs:4739](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/commands.rs#L4739) calls this while `AppState` and workers still hold database connections; restart occurs only afterward. The database enables a 256 MB mmap at [db.rs:177](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/crates/omera-storage/src/db.rs#L177).

With a synthetic active WAL connection, this Windows build fails with `Failed to replace live database ... user-mapped section open (os error 1224)`. No real database was restored. On systems allowing the copy, the source path still has active connections/WAL and non-atomic replacement risk; corruption or WAL contamination was not demonstrated on this host. Local restore already uses `recovery::stage_restore`, so cloud restore should use the same lifecycle.

## Environment and evidence

- Baseline: Omera 0.4.3, `dev` at [`bdac8fb`](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/commit/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5); SQLite schema 15.
- Review host: Windows; the inspected application was launched from the repository root with `pnpm run tauri dev`.
- Evidence strength is stated above. For code-confirmed scenarios, the steps below describe a targeted validation scenario rather than a completed end-to-end reproduction. Remote-provider, destructive real-library and cross-platform scenarios were not exercised.

## Reproduction or validation scenario

1. Create a temporary SQLite database using `Database::connect`, leaving its WAL-enabled connection open.
2. Create a different snapshot using `create_cloud_snapshot` with the LocalPath provider.
3. Call `restore_cloud_snapshot` for the active path while the first connection is alive.

## Expected behavior

Restore is staged and activated before opening SQLite connections; the current database remains recoverable on failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Use the existing staged restore lifecycle and activate before connections/workers start.
- [ ] Validate integrity, schema and foreign keys; create a consistent, verified rollback snapshot.
- [ ] Test active WAL, Windows mmap, interrupted activation, failed rollback creation and restart recovery.

## Related work and scope

Related closed issues: #98. This report describes the remaining behavior on the baseline above and does not assume that every earlier fix is absent.

Implementation must respect the lead-owned persistence, file-safety, migration or update-trust boundaries in [ENGINEERING_HANDOFF.md](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/docs/ENGINEERING_HANDOFF.md). Use synthetic fixtures and preserve source data. Any implementation PR should target `dev`.

```rust
    #[test]
    fn cloud_restore_must_survive_active_wal_connection() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let active_path = dir.path().join("active.db");
        let active = Database::connect(&active_path).unwrap();
        active.add_folder("active-before-checkpoint").unwrap();
        active.connection().execute_batch("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);").unwrap();
        active.add_folder("active-in-wal").unwrap();
```

### Problem Description

In `src/components/SettingsModal.vue`, several user preferences are persisted to `localStorage` in `saveSettings()`:
- `berry_default_view`: Default view mode (`"grid"` vs `"table"`)
- `berry_blur_nsfw`: Default blur on sensitive / 18+ content
- `berry_card_badges`: Show / hide card badges (format, favorite, nsfw)
- `berry_autoscan`: Automatically scan indexed folders on startup

However, these stored configurations are not wired up to `App.vue` or `VirtualGrid.vue`:
1. `App.vue`: `viewMode` is hardcoded to `ref<"grid" | "table">("grid")` without reading `berry_default_view` on initialization, and switching view modes via `SortBar` does not persist back to `localStorage`.
2. `VirtualGrid.vue`: NSFW blur is always applied (`file.is_nsfw && !revealedNsfw.has(file.path)`), ignoring the `berry_blur_nsfw` setting.
3. `VirtualGrid.vue`: Card badges are always rendered without checking `berry_card_badges`.
4. `App.vue`: `onMounted()` does not check `berry_autoscan` to trigger incremental background scans for registered folders.

### Proposed Solution

1. Initialize `viewMode` in `App.vue` from `localStorage.getItem("berry_default_view")` and update `localStorage` when changed.
2. Pass `blurNsfwDefault` and `showCardBadges` as props (or via a reactive settings store) to `VirtualGrid.vue`.
3. Implement optional background startup scan in `App.vue`'s `onMounted()` when `berry_autoscan !== "false"`.
title: [Settings] User preferences in SettingsModal are not connected to App and VirtualGrid components
